category: 3D model repository / maker marketplace — the strongest find in this niche

free_tier.stated: No published account quota and no published upload cap. Verified live object: a single 1,036,822,737 B (1.037 GB) STL served from files.printables.com. Also verified a model holding 29 files totalling 404.3 MB, and one holding six ZIPs of 62.5/167.5/208.5/65.0/98.8/118.6 MB. 'Other files' accepts ZIP, so arbitrary payloads ride inside an archive; and a single model accepts 1335+ files (forum report of a user hitting UI limits, not a storage limit).

egress.terms: Backed by Google Cloud Storage (x-goog-* headers), fronted by files.printables.com with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000` and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. No egress cap published, no paywall on download, no account needed to download.

interface_detail: Undocumented but stable public GraphQL: POST https://api.printables.com/graphql/ with no auth. `print(id:N){ name stls{id name fileSize} otherFiles{id name fileSize} downloadPacks{...} }` to enumerate; then mutation `getDownloadLink(id, printId, source:"model_detail", fileType:"stl"|"other")` returns `{ok, output:{link}}`.
tooling: Plain HTTP + JSON. Working Python/curl one-liner proven this session. No SDK needed. gid/uid path component is an opaque UUID, not a signature.
chaining: The returned link is a plain GCS object URL with NO signature and NO expiry field that is enforced (headers showed `expires: Fri, 06 Mar 2026` — a date already in the past — and the object still served on 2026-10-21, i.e. rule 9: the signature field is not a gate). Hot-linkable behind Cloudflare with zero origin egress cost. Object keys are enumerable per model, so a shard-and-replicate writer can treat each model as a bucket.
limits_note: per-object-cap: 1.037 GB observed (no stated ceiling found — the '1 GB' in that model's own title is the author's description, not a platform limit). Write is normal account signup; no curator. Download is anonymous. RANGE VERIFIED: `Range: bytes=100-199` returned `HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content`, `Content-Range: bytes 100-199/1036822737`, 100 bytes — so resumable/ranged GET works (this is NOT the RepOD case).

identity_cost.detail: email address and a password, or a Google, Apple or Facebook sign-in: the account article says to register or log in with Google, Apple or Facebook, or to choose Create an account at the bottom to use an email or password, then confirm the account from the sent email. No card and no phone number appear in that flow.

reliability_note: Terms 2.9 states plainly 'PRINTABLES does not serve as data storage' and disclaims liability for deletion, so durability is unguaranteed. The signup page answers a Cloudflare bot challenge to an unauthenticated fetch; the email signup is documented by Prusa's own account article.

extras.agent_focus: Print-on-demand, media and fulfilment platforms that host your uploads permanently and serve them cheaply. The question for every candidate was NOT 'can I upload' (all of them accept uploads) but: does the platform serve my ORIGINAL bytes back, unsigned, indefinitely, from a CDN I can hot-link? POD image hosts (Redbubble/Printful/Printify/Society6/Threadless/Zazzle/Etsy) all re-encode, cap at 20-300 MB and gate the write behind account setup — they are inverted (tiny ingress, no egress). The value in this niche is the DIGITAL-PRODUCT fulfilment layer and the 3D-model repositories, which are the two places where arbitrary file types survive ingest at GB scale.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
